title: Managers risk losing job to AI
full_text:
Almost half of Australian managers are exposed to AI disruption, with one in five at significant risk of job loss.
The 2026 B-Suite Benchmarks – Australia’s only comprehensive study of managers – has revealed 47 per cent of middle managers are not behaving in a way that could move them beyond the space that AI could automate.
Melbourne-based middle management expert Rebecca Houghton said leaders who are operating in “order taker mode” are at risk of being replaced by AI.
“It’s less about the work you’re doing and it’s more about the choice you’re making as a middle manager,” the BoldHR founder said.
“I think people who are responsible for any repeatable processes, people who are in spaces where quality and consistency is really important, these are the people that need to be AI gurus.” Ms Houghton said managers looking to survive the AI era should learn to use the software to their advantage and ensure that they are displaying these skills openly. She said it was vital workers were not only good at their job, but being seen in their role and generating tangible influence.
